surface-chrome.purpose: Tab strip, toolbars, table head, group and code headers.

surface-sunken.purpose: Query, variables and SDL code bodies.

surface-hover.purpose: Hover on rows, tabs, buttons, menu options.

selection.purpose: Selected row / type / active pill while the list is focused.

selection-idle.purpose: Selected row when its list is not focused.

divider.purpose: Every 1px region split and column rule; resting input border.

raised-border.purpose: Menu and dialog edge; kbd border; scrollbar thumb.

devtools-blue.purpose: Active tab, primary button, links, checkbox accent.

record-red.purpose: Recording circle, Intercepting status, live infobar dot.

awaiting-amber.purpose: Awaiting retry state; no-patterns warning; warning status.

error-red.purpose: Not in registry, errors, destructive confirm.

live-wash.purpose: Interception infobar and warning toast background.

update-flash.purpose: Start colour of the resolve-in-place row flash.

extensions.colorNotes: Canonical values are light-dark() pairs in frontend/css/tokens.css; tonalRamp is synthesized in OKLCH from the light value. Dark mode flips color-scheme only (frontend/css/theme-dark.css). prefers-contrast: more strengthens divider and ink-secondary.

title.purpose: Detail operation name, empty-state and dialog titles. Largest UI text (13px).

body.purpose: Default for all interface text at DevTools 12px.

label.purpose: Operation names, state words, column heads, primary/record buttons. Emphasis by weight 500.

code.purpose: Query, variables and SDL bodies; wraps, never scrolls horizontally.

code-small.purpose: Hashes, times, patterns, endpoint URLs, group headers, schema type names, inline code.

density.name: compact
density.purpose: Dense tables; set via data-density="compact" and applied automatically at max-height 460px.

shadows.name: shadow-menu
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: settings menu, toasts, dialog panel.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Focus indicator (an outline, not a shadow); inset -1px/-2px on rows, tabs, lists and code.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Standard easing for state transitions, the row flash and toast entry.

motion.name: row-updated
motion.purpose: Signature resolve-in-place flash; reduced motion swaps it for a 1px resolved-green inset outline.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: Record dot in the live infobar pulses three times, then rests.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below: detail pane overlays the list; Hash column, Patterns label and pane descriptions drop.

breakpoints.name: very-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below: Time column, resolved count and toolbar separators drop; schema type list 140px.

narrative.overview:
APQ Debugger is built to be mistaken for a panel Chrome shipped itself. It sits beside Network and Elements, so it takes their system wholesale: 12px system UI type, monospace for anything machine-made (hashes, queries, URLs, timestamps), white and grey-100 surfaces (dark: #202124 / #292a2d) split by 1px dividers, Google blue for selection, focus and the one primary action, record red, a yellow infobar while traffic is being rewritten, and green reserved for a resolved hash. Familiarity is the design goal; personality is spent only on state changes.

The structure is the DevTools canon: a tab strip (Requests, Schema, settings gear and session status at the right), a per-view toolbar, an optional collapsible patterns pane, an infobar when interception or passive mode is on, then a dense single-line data table with a detail pane that appears only after selection. In the detail pane the recovered query is the largest, most readable thing on screen, wrapped and syntax-coloured in DevTools Sources colours. The system rejects the editorial card-and-metric dashboard and the permanent settings sidebar that preceded it.

Density is a working constraint, not a preference: the panel is often docked about 400px tall. Comfortable matches DevTools' default row height (24px), Compact its dense tables (20px), and Compact switches on by itself when the panel is 460px tall or less. The one signature moment is a pending APQ row resolving in place, its state flipping to Resolved under the DevTools "updated" flash.
keyCharacteristics: System UI 12px for interface, ui-monospace for code, hashes, URLs and times; no bundled or network fonts.
Flat in-flow surfaces separated by 1px dividers and tonal steps (surface vs chrome vs sunken).
Blue means selection, focus or primary; red means recording; yellow means traffic is being rewritten; green means resolved.
Every request state is a word plus a glyph shape, never colour alone.
Single-line 24px (20px compact) table rows with column dividers.
Every colour defined once with light-dark(); dark mode only flips color-scheme.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each signal colour has exactly one job: blue is selection, focus and the primary action; red is recording; yellow is live rewriting or a warning; green is a resolved hash. A colour never borrows another's meaning.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Rewriting Rule
rules.body: The yellow infobar is visible if and only if the debugger is attached and rewriting matching traffic; it names the patterns in monospace and carries Stop. Passive mode gets the blue infobar instead, because nothing is modified.

rules.name: The Define-Once Rule
rules.body: Every colour is declared once in tokens.css as `light-dark(light, dark)`. Dark mode is a `color-scheme` flip in theme-dark.css (explicit `data-theme` wins; otherwise the system preference). No component redeclares a colour per theme.

rules.name: The Machine-Text Rule
rules.body: Anything the machine produced (hash, URL, pattern, timestamp, query, type name) is set in the monospace stack; anything a person reads as interface is in system-ui. Numbers that update in place use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Flat Ramp Rule
rules.body: The ramp spans 11px to 13px. Hierarchy comes from weight (400/500/600), colour (ink vs ink-secondary) and position, never from display sizes. Sentence case throughout; no uppercase tracking, no eyebrows.

rules.name: The Docked-First Rule
rules.body: Design for the panel docked about 400px tall: no chrome may cost more than one toolbar row plus the optional infobar before data rows begin.

rules.name: The Overlays-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "floating above the panel". Rows, panes, toolbars, code blocks and infobars never carry one.

dos: Do take every colour from tokens.css and add new ones there as `light-dark(light, dark)` pairs with text at 4.5:1 and meaningful indicators at 3:1 in both themes.
Do separate regions with 1px dividers and the surface / chrome / sunken tonal steps.
Do express every request state as a word plus a glyph shape, using the vocabulary in `request-state.js`.
Do set hashes, URLs, patterns, times and code in the monospace stack, and counts in tabular numerals.
Do keep controls at the density heights (22/20px controls, 24/20px rows) so compact and the short-dock auto-compact keep working.
Do keep the query block wrapped and dominant in the detail pane; the recovered query is the largest readable thing on screen.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion fallback that keeps the meaning (the resolve flash becomes a green outline).
Do support forced colours: selection maps to Highlight/HighlightText and floating layers get a CanvasText border.
donts: Don't add shadows to in-flow surfaces; the overlay shadow is for menus, toasts and dialogs only.
Don't use green for anything except a resolved hash, or yellow except live interception and warnings.
Don't signal state with colour alone.
Don't load fonts, icons or scripts from the network, or ship a display face; the platform system-ui and ui-monospace stacks are the type system.
Don't reintroduce the editorial card-and-metric dashboard, a permanent settings sidebar, uppercase tracked eyebrows or display numerals.
Don't redeclare colours for dark mode; flip `color-scheme` only.
Don't let the query scroll horizontally; it wraps.
